title: NeoForge's game setup is paid once per machine, not once per mod
text: NeoForge's first setup for a game version (NeoForm: decompile, inject, transformSource, recompile) ran in each mod folder: on Jon's PC on 2026-11-08 Notes and Zombie Apocalypse each began it for 1.21.6, its steps took 12, 24, 34 and 22+ minutes under fairshare's idle priority, and both were killed. A second mod on the same NeoForge and Minecraft version must reuse the first one's setup and start compiling within minutes.
result: Every forward NeoForge port now moves to the same NeoGradle (the newest 7.x), so NeoGradle's own cross-project cache (~/.gradle/caches/ng_execute, keyed by task class, inputs and file contents, not by folder) serves every mod on that version. Zombie Apocalypse 1.21.1 → 1.21.6 right after Notes ran 0 NeoForm steps and made 0 cache entries; its whole port took 30 s. The cold setup itself takes 137 s on an idle 8-core machine (decompile 33 s, recompile 30 s): the hours on the PC were the PC starved, not the work. bench/neoform_steps.py times each step and counts the cache entries a build made.
